motion: Fixed camera on a tripod, framing unchanged. From the first moment, a warm evening breeze stirs the bamboo on the left: the fine leaves flutter and the tall stems lean gently and sway back. The palm in the middle rocks its fronds slowly. The low sun behind the bamboo flickers and shimmers as leaves pass across it, little bursts of golden light breaking through and closing again. Far off, thin haze drifts slowly sideways over the layered hills. The thatched roofs at the bottom stay solid and still. The whole upper part of the frame remains a smooth, plain apricot sky, evenly lit from edge to edge. Calm, quiet, real footage at golden hour.

A very slow, steady sideways glide to the right begins straight away, so the bamboo and palm shift gently against the distant hills, a soft parallax. At the same time the leaves rustle in a light wind and sunlight glitters through the gaps in the bamboo, the sun's glow pulsing softly as branches move over it. Mist hangs and creeps along the far valleys. The thatched roofs stay still. The top of the frame is open, cloudless sky the whole time, a clean warm gradient. Peaceful, slow, natural evening light.

From the first frame the camera pushes in slowly and smoothly toward the carved wooden sign, keeping it centred. Around it, the big banana leaves in the foreground rock gently in a breeze and the bamboo behind sways. Dappled sunlight slides across the wood, spots of light drifting over the grain. The sign and its bamboo frame stay fixed and solid; the white lettering stays sharp and identical: DETOX FROM MATERIALISM, WEEKEND RETREAT, £3,000. Quiet jungle morning, real footage.

The palm fronds at the top right sway in a gust right away, and their shadows flicker across the sign so the light on the wood brightens and dims in soft patches. The ferns and banana leaves at the bottom nod and tremble. The camera eases forward very slowly, a gentle creep toward the sign over the whole clip. The sign holds perfectly still on its posts, its painted words crisp and unchanged, exactly as written. Warm, humid, unhurried.

Fixed camera, framing unchanged. The man in the navy gilet in the foreground sits cross-legged with his eyes shut, his fist at his mouth; immediately his lips murmur quickly behind his hand as he whispers into the phone tucked in his shirt cuff, his head bowing a fraction toward his wrist, shoulders hunched. Behind him on the right, softly out of focus, the woman in white keeps her palms open on her knees and speaks slowly and calmly, her hands lifting slightly with the words. The woman on the left stays perfectly still with closed eyes and closed lips, breathing gently, and the guest at the far right edge stays still with closed lips. Soft morning light, leaves moving faintly outside the bamboo arches.

Camera creeps in very slowly toward the man in the navy gilet. Straight away he presses his knuckles closer to his mouth and his lips move in a small, urgent whisper behind his hand, eyes kept shut, brow tightening slightly, as he talks into the phone hidden at his cuff; he glances nowhere, keeps the pose of meditation. In the soft background the woman in white gently turns her open palms upward and speaks in a slow, soothing rhythm, a serene look on her face. The other guests sit motionless, eyes closed, lips closed, chests rising softly. Bamboo hall, warm daylight, real footage.

Fixed camera. The bronze gong behind has just been struck: from the first frame its face trembles and sways slightly on its cord, a shimmer of light rippling across the polished metal. The woman in white keeps her eyes closed with a peaceful expression, lips closed, and slowly lowers the felt mallet in her hand. At the same time the man in the balaclava pushes the card machine a few inches closer to the camera with both gloved hands, then holds it there, quite still and patient. His navy knitted balaclava stays exactly the same: the white ring around the face, the small red triangle over his left eye. The navy roll-neck covers his neck and the black gloves meet his navy cuffs at the wrists. The machine's keypad and screen stay unchanged. Leaves stir in the garden behind.

Fixed camera. Immediately the man in the balaclava extends the card machine toward the lens in one smooth, unhurried move, stops, and holds it out, steady, his masked head tilting a tiny degree as if waiting. Behind him the gong is still ringing visibly: its surface quivers and the whole disc rocks gently back and forth, catching the light. The woman in white stands serene, eyes closed, lips closed, breathing slowly, the mallet hanging at her side. His navy balaclava keeps its white ring and red triangle over his left eye exactly as they are; navy roll-neck up to the chin, black gloves sealed against his navy cuffs. The keypad stays identical. Bright tropical daylight, real footage.

A very slow, smooth push-in toward the large grey stone on the nearest white plinth, starting at once and continuing gently for the whole clip. A soft glint of light travels slowly across the stone's speckled surface. The bamboo stems in the vase quiver very slightly. Everything else stays still and silent in the empty wooden shop. The small price card stays readable as £80, the mug reads NON-ATTACHMENT £24, and the sign above the door reads EXIT THROUGH GIFT SHOP, all unchanged. Hushed, warm, real footage.

From the start the camera drifts forward very slowly along the shelf, closing in on the second stone in the row, the nearest stone sliding gently toward the frame edge. Warm light shifts a little across the wooden wall as if a cloud passed outside, and the stones gleam faintly as it moves. The bamboo leaves in the vase tremble. The shop stays empty and perfectly quiet. All printed words stay sharp and exactly the same: EXIT THROUGH GIFT SHOP, NON-ATTACHMENT £24, £80. Calm, still, expensive.

Locked camera, framing unchanged. From the first moment a strong wind moves through the tall trees at the top: branches bend and leaves stream sideways in long waves, the bushes behind him rustling. The old groundskeeper sits on the mossy rock, gazing up at the treetops, relaxed and content. After a moment he lifts the tin cup with both hands, takes one slow sip of tea, and lowers it to rest on his knee again, still looking up at the trees. His cap stays on. The wheelbarrow and the flask on the grass stay still. Overcast daylight, real footage, quiet and calm.

Locked camera. Immediately a gust sweeps across the treetops from right to left, the high leaves streaming and the slender trunks swaying; the hedge beneath shivers. The groundskeeper's eyes follow it slowly across the canopy, his head turning a little, a faint peaceful look on his weathered face. He breathes out, raises the cup in both hands for a slow sip, then lowers it and keeps watching the trees. The wheelbarrow, the flask and the thatched roof behind stay still. Grey, soft light, gentle and unhurried.

Locked camera, framing unchanged. From the first frame the little terrier, standing with its front paws on the old man's knee, wags its tail quickly from side to side, mouth closed. The groundskeeper scratches the top of its head with slow fingers while still looking up at the trees with a small, contented smile, his cup held in his other hand. Above, the wind streams through the tall trees, leaves rippling and branches swaying. The wheelbarrow and flask stay still. Overcast daylight, real footage, warm and calm.

Locked camera. Straight away the terrier pushes its head up into the old man's hand, its tail wagging hard and its ears flicking, front paws staying on his knee, mouth closed. He rubs gently behind its ears and along its head, never looking down, his gaze still lifted to the swaying treetops, his small smile deepening slightly. The tall trees bend and their leaves stream in the wind; the hedge rustles. His cup stays in his other hand, the flask and wheelbarrow stay still. Soft grey light, gentle and quiet.
